scenario: A SaaS provider encrypts storage, but the customer misconfigures federation and exposes records.
best_action: Map controls to the service model and remediate customer identity configuration first.
must_reason: shared responsibility does not disappear in SaaS
provider assurance differs from customer configuration
trap: Treating the provider as accountable for every control.

scenario: Two providers meet features and price; one lacks tested export and deletion mechanisms.
best_action: Evaluate reversibility, portability, evidence access, and exit requirements before selection.

scenario: A confidential-computing service is proposed for sensitive AI inference.
best_action: Threat-model which data states and trust boundaries it protects and verify attestation operations.
must_reason: data in use versus transit/at rest
trap: Assuming a TEE makes the entire workload trusted.

scenario: A retention timer expires while litigation counsel has placed the dataset on legal hold.
best_action: Preserve the data and documented hold, overriding normal deletion until authorized release.
trap: Deleting because the ordinary retention period ended.

scenario: A global object store contains restricted records whose residency labels are incomplete.
best_action: Discover, classify, map locations and flows, then enforce placement before further processing.
trap: Encrypting data while ignoring jurisdiction and processing location.

scenario: A tenant requests proof that cryptographic erasure rendered archived replicas inaccessible.
best_action: Correlate key destruction with asset, replica, backup, retention, and provider evidence.
trap: Presenting a delete API response as complete destruction proof.

scenario: A risk cannot be eliminated without abandoning a critical cloud service.
best_action: Quantify residual risk, select a documented treatment, and obtain accountable acceptance when appropriate.

scenario: A regional failure occurs and replicas exist, but recovery exceeds the business tolerance.
best_action: Compare observed recovery to approved RTO/RPO and test the full dependency restoration sequence.
trap: Equating replication with a tested recovery capability.

scenario: An IaaS guest remains vulnerable despite a provider statement that the infrastructure is patched.
best_action: Distinguish provider hypervisor/facility duties from customer guest OS and workload duties.
trap: Extending provider patch responsibility into customer-controlled guests.

scenario: A dependency passes functional tests but its provenance and license are unknown.
best_action: Quarantine release pending supply-chain verification and an accountable risk decision.
trap: Treating functional correctness as software assurance.

scenario: An API accepts valid tokens but allows users to enumerate other tenants' objects.
best_action: Enforce object-level authorization and add abuse-case tests at every request.
trap: Adding stronger authentication without fixing authorization.

scenario: A release has SAST findings, one exploitable runtime configuration, and no threat-model update.
best_action: Risk-rank evidence, block the exploitable condition, and update the secure-SDLC record.
trap: Counting scanner findings instead of evaluating exploitability and impact.

scenario: Logs show possible exfiltration, but clocks differ and an administrator wants to alter the source VM.
best_action: Coordinate incident containment with forensic preservation and normalized chronology.
trap: Making unrecorded changes that destroy evidence.

scenario: A critical patch exists for an HA service with no maintenance window.
best_action: Use risk-based emergency change, staged redundancy, rollback, and verification.
trap: Choosing either indefinite delay or simultaneous fleet patching.

scenario: A cloud incident affects customers and may trigger regulatory notice.
best_action: Use the communications matrix to send accurate, authorized, audience-specific updates.
trap: Publishing speculative root cause to every audience.

scenario: A regulator demands records stored under a conflicting foreign localization law.
best_action: Escalate to qualified counsel, preserve relevant data, and document jurisdiction and authority.

scenario: A provider offers a clean assurance report whose scope excludes the service and region being purchased.
best_action: Treat the report as insufficient and obtain scoped evidence or mitigate the gap.
trap: Treating the provider logo or report title as coverage.

scenario: A contract promises 99.99% uptime but is silent on data return, deletion, audit, and breach coordination.
best_action: Negotiate operationally testable clauses before commitment.
trap: Using availability SLA as a substitute for the full security agreement.
